tool.name: csrf_check
tool.description:
Probe a state-changing form for CSRF posture weaknesses. Replays the form with each of the standard CSRF-bypass mutations and flags variants the server accepts.
**Probe matrix** (each compared against a baseline submission with the legitimate token):
**Token-bypass family** (only when token field is detected/supplied): - `token_removed` — omit the CSRF field entirely - `token_empty` — send empty value - `token_mutated` — flip the last character - `token_random` — replace with CSPRNG-random of similar length
**Token replay** — same legitimate token submitted twice (one-time-ness check)
**Origin/Referer family**: - `origin_attacker` — `Origin: https://strix-<nonce>.evil.example` - `origin_removed` — omit `Origin` header (presence-only validators bypassed by no-header) - `origin_null` — `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes / data: URIs) - `referer_attacker` — `Referer: https://strix-<nonce>.evil.example/`
**Double-submit cookie family** (only when token cookie name is supplied/detected): - `double_submit_mismatch` — token cookie left intact; form-field token mutated. Accepted = the cookie/form comparison is broken.
**Token field auto-detection** lexicon: `csrfmiddlewaretoken` (Django), `authenticity_token` (Rails), `__RequestVerificationToken` (ASP.NET), `_token` (Laravel), `_csrf` (Express csurf / NestJS), `csrf_token`, `csrf`, `anti_csrf_token`, `csrftoken`, `xsrf_token`. Override via `token_field` parameter.
**Token cookie auto-detection** lexicon: `csrftoken`, `csrf-token`, `XSRF-TOKEN`, `_csrf`, `_xsrf`, `csrf`. Override via `token_cookie` parameter.
**Acceptance heuristic**: same status class (2xx/3xx) AND body length within ±25% of baseline AND not a stock 401/403/405/429.
**Per-class dedup** so 4 token-bypass mutations emit at most one "missing token validation" finding, not four.
Severity: - **High** CWE-352 — token removed/empty/mutated/random accepted; OR `Origin: attacker` accepted; OR double-submit-cookie mismatch accepted. - **Medium** CWE-352 — `Origin` removed accepted; OR `Origin: null` accepted; OR `Referer: attacker` accepted (without other CSRF defense). - **Low** CWE-352 — token replay accepted (one-time-ness violation).
Skip cases: - Baseline submission with the legitimate token returns non-2xx/3xx → `inconclusive=True` (the form description is wrong; operator needs to fix the field map or the auth). - `--exclude-path` blocks the URL → graceful no-op.
**Safety**: - All probes are sent with the operator's supplied form fields and cookies; no extra exfiltration vectors. - Probe attacker host gets unique random `strix-<nonce>.evil.example` prefix per run for log auditability. - 64KiB response body cap. - Composes with cluster-A safety (`--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` / `--auth-*`). - All findings carry severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (double-submit cookie + per-form unique CSRF token; reject requests without `Origin` or with `Origin` not in allow-list; reject mismatched / re-used tokens; rotate token on each form render; use `__Host-` cookie prefix for double-submit) and `verification_status=needs_review` since `2xx` doesn't always mean the side-effect happened (framework may return `200` for unhandled requests).
**Caveat for destructive forms**: this tool DOES dispatch the form's state-changing request (multiple times). Don't run against production unless the form is a non-destructive read endpoint — use staging or a dedicated test account.

parameter.name: target_url
parameter.description: URL the form posts to. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Examples: `https://app.example.com/profile/update`, `https://api.example.com/v1/transfers`.

parameter.name: method
parameter.description: HTTP method. Default `POST`. Use `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` for REST APIs, or `GET` for state-changing-via-GET endpoints (rare but real).

parameter.name: fields
parameter.description: Form field name → value map. Should include the CSRF token field with its current legitimate value. The token field is auto-detected via the framework lexicon (override with `token_field`).

parameter.name: token_field
parameter.description: Override for the CSRF token field name (when auto-detection is wrong or the field uses a custom name).

parameter.name: token_cookie
parameter.description: Override for the CSRF token cookie name. When set, the double-submit-cookie mismatch probe is enabled. Auto-detected from the `cookies` map via the framework lexicon if not supplied.

parameter.name: cookies
parameter.description: Cookie name → value map sent with each request. Cluster-A `--auth-cookie` env layers on top. Set the CSRF token cookie here when probing double-submit pattern.

parameter.name: content_type
parameter.description: Override the default `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Set to `application/json` for JSON APIs.

parameter.name: extra_headers
parameter.description: Additional headers (e.g. CSRF tokens carried in headers like `X-CSRF-Token`).

returns.description:
{success, target_url, target_host, method, token_field, token_cookie, baseline: {status, status_class, body_length, error?, skipped?}, probes: [{label, class_, status, body_length, accepted, finding_severity}, ...], findings_emitted, inconclusive?, reason?}.
The agent should follow up high-severity findings by manually verifying the side-effect actually happened (was the resource really updated? did the new value persist?) before treating the finding as confirmed exploitable — `2xx` doesn't always mean the server processed the request as intended.
